reviews.title: The single most annoying app on the planet to use
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this for over 4 years (not many options to use because the customization is at least nice) hoping and praying they’d learn to make the interface user friendly but more times than I can count they will add an update and move something for no reason and make it harder to access. Take logging your weight for example. There used to be a home page and you could just scroll down and log your weight, now it feels like you have to go through annoying hoops just to bring up your chart to see your progress for the week. Yes there’s the plus button then you log your weight, but if I want to see the graph, the steps involved have been increasingly more complicated than simply scrolling down. They also made logging food weirder. Before you could tap a meal like breakfast and log food and see your calories and macros. Now for some reason after I log my food, I can’t compare the macros of my meals to each other because I have to tap breakfast and view the macros for just breakfast then hit back and repeat for all my meals. 

BUT THE SINGLE MOST ANNOYING THING OF ALL IS IT NON STOP LOGS YOU OUT OF THE APP. I pay for premium BECAUE I use the app everyday. I love premium because I can customize my calories and macros. But what is the ****ing point if it logs me out of the app each time I stop using it. Which isn’t a big problem alone but not only does it log you out, logging back in immediately logs you out about 5 times until it finally decides to open and guess what? ALL MY MACROS AND CALORIE GOALS ARE RESET EVERY SINGLE TIME!!!!! This isn’t a rare occurrence either this happens multiple times a day, randomly throughout the week, then it’ll function fine, then it’ll randomly reset my goals again and again and again and again and again. I’ve tried deleting and redownloading the app, I’ve already logged out and logged back in a million times over the course of 4 years, and the issue still persists. 

Please fix the app. For now highly recommend choosing something else. Even just using paper would be less stressful which I will be doing from now on since I have to rewrite my macros and calorie goals every day anyways

reviews.title: This WAS a good app
reviews.text:
I have been using this App for years. At the beginning it helped me through my weight-loss journey, and it was fantastic. I attributed my success, in part, to this app. Since then it has helped me maintain a healthy weight, and improve my macros intake in order to get a balanced diet and achieve better results from my training. 

Then Under Armour bought the app. This is when it went downhill. Since that time, every new update is worse than the previous one. It has come to the point that the app quits abruptly, takes the longest time to add foods, wrongly calculates your calories consumed/remaining (or takes a long time to update them after inputting foods), and worst of all, it drains my phone’s battery like crazy. I used the app for 35 sec, which only gave me time to input 2 items, and battery went from 82% to 76%. As soon as I closed the app the battery drain stopped (I have downloaded videos and articles over the past 20 min and my battery is at 72%).

I am saddened, to say the least, that such a great app has turned to be a piece of junk. It became part of my routine and now it is unusable. Time to move on, I guess.

——————
Update on 2026-10-29:

I continued to use the app since my last review. I guess losing a 15-year history of dieting was too much to handle. Some updated corrected the sluggishness and battery drain.

This latest update, with the interface redesign, is too much to digest. Now the app has become completely unusable. I can’t get all the relevant information on one screen; have to continuously click or scroll to find one or other info… it’s a complete waste of time. Logging foods and exercises is already a time-consuming activity. You would think the goal should be to make it easier, not exponentially more difficult. Either you change or I’m out. And I know I’m not alone. Many people hate your new interface. It’s time to listen.

I’ve been using MyFitnessPal for so many years now, and it’s honestly amazing to see how much the app has grown. You guys are one of the OGs when it comes to tracking calories and nutrition.

One thing I’ve been thinking about is how cool it would be if MyFitnessPal came out with its own smart food scale. There are already some really good food scales out there that connect to calorie-tracking apps, and I feel like this is something MyFitnessPal could really take advantage of

Imagine having a food scale that connects directly to MyFitnessPal, where you can weigh your food and have the calories, protein, carbs, and fats automatically added to your food diary. It would make tracking so much easier.

I’ve also seen some really modern food scales with TFT color displays, and I think combining something like that with AI-powered features would be pretty cool. Especially if the scale could work with MyFitnessPal’s food database.

You guys already have such a huge community of people who use the app for their fitness and nutrition goals. I really think having your own food scale could be something worth looking into, and I wouldn’t be surprised if a lot of people would be interested in buying one.

Just an idea from someone who’s been using and appreciating the app for years. I would genuinely love to see you guys explore something like this

Not having an option to opt out of the AI features, while using the data input into the app to train the model and sell to advertisers, is the definition of a security risk. 

The UI is unintuitive. 

I have been a paid user for near on a decade off and on. And most recently went premium for the barcode scanning, which used to be free. This sounds very much like a cash grab using a database of millions of barcodes built by early adopters, profiting off the free labor provided by users. 

The fix is simple. 

OPTION 1 — Allow an opt out for the AI features, which would send the app back to a straight calorie diary again for those who want it. Resulting in a simple UI

OPTION 2 — provide an API key for users to access for those who do wish to use AI for insights and other things. Removing the security risk of having an AI within the app itself and simplifying the UI.

reviews.title: Please prioritize usability alongside the redesign
reviews.text:
I use MyFitnessPal every day and am a Premium subscriber. While the updated mobile UI looks more polished, several common actions now require more taps to enter the exact same information. For an app built around frequent, repetitive data entry, adding extra steps to routine logging makes the experience noticeably more frustrating.

At the same time, the desktop experience, particularly recipe creation and editing, feels extremely outdated. Ironically, I prefer creating recipes in the mobile app because the workflow is better, even though recipe editing is exactly the kind of task I’d rather do on a computer with a full keyboard.

I’d love to see the best of both: keep the improved visual design on mobile without burying frequently used actions behind additional taps, and bring the desktop recipe tools up to the usability standard of the mobile app.

As a paying, daily user, these small workflow changes add up quickly. I’m happy to see the app being actively updated, but I’d love to see usability prioritized alongside appearance.

reviews.title: Disappointed by predatory paywalls and toxic diet logic
reviews.text:
This app continues to get farther away from where it started - it was the best. The new update forces free users into a toxic, outdated "eat back your exercise calories" model. Every time I move, my macro goals shift automatically, treating food like a transaction or a reward for working out. It’s incredibly weight-watchers-esque and mentally unhealthy. The fact that MyFitnessPal forces this fluctuating target on free users—and locks the simple ability to freeze your goals behind a $20/month premium paywall—is predatory.
There is literally an automatic calorie/macro adjustment every time a free user logs exercise or steps. This is an unhealthy, obsessive way to track food. The goals change constantly throughout the day, creating a frustratingly moving target. Turning this stressful feature off shouldn’t be a Premium feature, nor should we have to disable steps and fitness tracking in the app to stop this outdated model.  Disappointed to see this app prioritize aggressive paywalls over user mental health.
